title: Settlement mismatch incident
summary: Find and fix a bug with the team's memory and the rule chain
story: The nightly settlement reconciliation for 18 April 2026 failed its integrity check: the scheme fee totals differ from the card schemes' own settlement totals by a few pence, and the settlement file is held for manual review.

card.about: A bug fix done the way a regulated payments team has to do it. The chat explains the problem, the rules it touches and the recommendation in plain language; the code stays in the IDE. The presenter reviews the proposed change as a diff, applies it and runs the tests until they pass, and the system writes an evidence record that names the rules cited, the test run and the model that wrote the change.
card.scenario: Priya Nair picks up INC-2026-0419 first thing. Finance Operations has held the 18 April settlement file because the scheme fee totals are a few pence short of what Visa and Mastercard settled. The reconciliation job accumulates fees in binary floating point and truncates to pence; the team's own 2024 penny-drift post-mortem and the Payments Engineering Standard both say money is exact decimal, rounded once per transaction. The fix is small; what matters is that it traces to the standard and the regulation and leaves a record an auditor can read.

the corporate rule above the standards: governance and internal control, accurate charges, daily reconciliation, breaks resolved before release, testing of changes and evidence (clauses 4.1 to 4.10)
the requirements the faulty code breaks (PAY-012, PAY-013), the integrity check that caught it (PAY-014, PAY-015) and the change and audit rules for the fix (PAY-020, PAY-030)
what the fix must ship with: reconciliation tests whose figures come from the fixture (TST-004), a regression test that failed first (TST-006) and the evidence (TST-008)
the team's own memory: the same bug in the 2024 refund fee batch, a first fix that was also wrong, and the lessons (L1 to L4)
the team's decision: money is Decimal with a scale of two, rounded half up once per transaction (D1, D3)

outputs: A corrected reconciler that uses exact decimal arithmetic, with the existing tests passing
The test run captured with its command, exit code and output, shown in the IDE
An evidence record under compliance/records naming the rules cited, the tests, the model and the files changed, approval pending
value: The fix is traceable to the standard and the regulation, not only to a developer's judgement
The team's own history is applied instead of relearnt, once the team layer is in the store
The use of AI on the change is itself recorded: model, thinking mode, tokens, time and sources
Reset and repeat: the demo runs from the same seed every time

talkTrack: Every team has incidents. What matters here is that the fix traces to the standard and the regulation, and that the team's past lesson is used rather than relearnt. Select the demo: the ticket and the code open in the IDE and the tests run once, failing as the ticket reports. Diagnose: the chat explains the cause and the rules behind it, layer by layer, in plain language, and the IDE highlights the faulty lines. Fix: the IDE shows the proposed change as a diff; apply it and run the tests until they pass. Record: the evidence record lists the rules, the test run and the model that wrote the change.
